shared_elements: rounded-corner rectangular cartouches or panels filled with curvilinear detail
anthropomorphic face with eye and mouth (large face in A; small head-signs within B)
densely packed low-relief carving covering the whole field
justification: A depicts a single massive anthropomorphic figure with a broad headdress, arms folded over the chest and a large circular pectoral disc, while B depicts nothing but a double column of rounded-square sign blocks packed with curvilinear infill; the only real correspondences are generic ones (discs, small faces embedded in ornament, dense low-relief covering the whole field) plus a comparable schematic convention of rounded outlines with tightly nested internal detail. The dominant difference is subject: one is a figural body with a coherent head-torso arrangement, the other a strictly gridded sequence of repeated sign-blocks with no figure at all.
